records.subagent_summary: Execution 148.176 scored 0 of 8. Three rollouts hit the 16384-token cap with no boxed answer; all five finishers split the two possible readings of the public value into separate outer cases, settled each reading first, then found that inside a fixed reading each speaker could compute the partner directly, called both cases contradictory, and boxed the same wrong value. No rollout ever built the per-private-value groups the incumbent asks for, because collapsing the reading up front makes every group a singleton. This edit spends the tokens freed by dropping the trailing clause (round 8 evidence: echoed only in verbatim recitation, never executed as a step) on the one concrete move the rollouts lacked - keep an unstated reading open inside the groups instead of fixing it first - at essentially the incumbent's length. Deferring an unstated role assignment until the constraints are applied helps any multi-reading problem.

Fresh rollouts (execution_id 148.177) scored 7/8. The single miss is the same failure this hint has shown for six rounds: it derived the correct locus quadratic and even verified three roots on it, then spent the rest of a 16384-token budget calling the unnormalized form an ellipse 55 times and hit the length cap having boxed nothing. All seven passing traces normalized the common square coefficient, completed the square, and boxed a value. Rounds 2 and 4 proved that appending a normalize/certify guard for that stall loses held-out, and rounds 5-8 proved compressing or deleting clauses loses too, so this edit changes only the final verb: 'extracting' becomes 'boxing', turning the last step from an internal derivation into a required visible commitment. It is the one instruction the failing trace lacked, costs zero tokens (70 vs 70), and every held-out problem needs a boxed answer.

Fresh rollouts scored 4/8. All four failures burned the full 16384-token budget chasing exact coordinates of tilted/rotated placements (13-55 tangency mentions, 24-39 'Alternatively' restarts each); three never closed the reasoning block and one closed at 99 percent of budget then restarted a fresh write-up and was truncated. Two failures had already reached the correct value by a rough bounding argument and abandoned it. The incumbent's symmetry clause is the inert part: 'symmetr' appears 0-8 times per trace and it is also wrong-footed here, since the quantity does depend on the free rotation, so it offers no exit from the tilted-case search. This edit swaps it for one executable exit rule - bound the tilted case in one line rather than computing it, and drop it when that bound cannot beat the value already held - which applies to any placement/extremum problem and lands at 166 tokens versus the incumbent's 169.

Fresh round-9 rollouts (execution 148.179) scored 4/8. Every clause of the incumbent is exercised by all eight rollouts, so nothing is inert; the four failures instead lose the already-derived product at the very end, reporting the per-polynomial cap, the menu size, or nothing at all after the token budget runs out. Five prior rounds tried patching the cap argument itself and held-out fell every time, so this edit leaves the technical core untouched and instead front-loads the bound-one-object-then-add-capacities plan so the total is the goal from the first line, generalises the differencing ban from polynomials to objects, and asks explicitly for the total to be boxed. It is shorter than the incumbent (150 vs 153 tokens).

Three of eight rollouts scored; four of five failures ended in finish_reason=length. The instructive failure obeyed every clause - pinned the constants, reduced to one unknown, solved, rejected the root repeating a known point - then built the last vertex by arithmetic on a known point instead of evaluating the defining equation there, and boxed that value. It believed it had "met every condition" after only the domain and non-degeneracy filters. The successes instead put each vertex back through the defining equation. So only the incumbent terminal test is retargeted from the vague "meeting every condition" to the executable "satisfying every equation"; the body is byte-identical and rounds 7 and 8 both lost by touching the relabel clause, so it is kept. Length is exactly at incumbent parity, 70 tokens.

Fresh rollouts scored 2/8. Four of the eight hit the token limit without ever boxing anything, and the failures again substituted a uniform guess (1/24, 1/16, 1/4, 1/2) or thrashed over whether the target outcome was reachable at all; the two rewarded rollouts did loosely price free binary steps as the hint directs. My own history says a box-and-stop clause was tried in rounds 4, 5 and 6 here and lost held-out every time, while strict lossless compression is the one mutation that ever won this slot (185 to 177 tokens, held-out 0.2125 to 0.25). So this repeats exactly that: same strategy, same clauses in the same order, nothing dropped, 177 to 170 tokens by eliding redundant words. A shorter prompt also leaves the 1.7B student more room to finish the state-by-state pricing it already starts.

Fresh round-9 rollouts scored 1/8. Two clauses are measurably dead. The closing 'Confirm on one more size, then commit' is never executed: no rollout attempts a fourth size and 'confirm' appears zero times outside the quoted hint. The prohibition sentence is worse than dead: all eight rollouts build the polynomial in x anyway and none echoes the ban, and the single winner reached the answer precisely by leaving the table for theory. Meanwhile six of eight hit the 16384-token cap with no boxed value. So I keep the shrink and ratio clauses the winner did use, delete both inert sentences, and spend the space on the winner's actual final move: fit one formula in n covering every computed entry with signs, substitute the given size, box it. 69 tokens versus the incumbent's 70.

Fresh round-9 rollouts scored 6/8; all eight ran the incumbent's machinery (gcd of the totals, divisors as candidate counts, percent applied to cost) and both failures were selection-only picks among candidates they had already listed. Patching that fork has lost held-out for me four times (rounds 2, 4, 6, 7), so I left it alone. The transfer signal in my history is elsewhere: my best held-out ever (0.1875) came from the one version that named the trigger words integer/whole/identical/equal, and held-out dropped to 0.15 in the very compression that deleted that list. This edit restores only that lexical trigger, so the divisibility step can fire on unseen wordings, and pays for it by tightening the tagging clause; it adds no rule and is shorter than the incumbent.

1/8 correct; the other seven all died on the 16384-token cap. Every rollout reached for the involution, so the ansatz wording is doing its job, but the two-layer notation 'f = L(g) with L(t) = s - t' is what they misparse: three unpacked it as the wrong composite q = s - p(s - x), one as f(f(x)) = g(x), and they burned their budget probing those dead ends before reverting to full composition coefficient matching. The single winner stated the ansatz in the direct form instead and finished in 8k tokens. So this is a byte-minimal lossless substitution: every other character of the incumbent is untouched, and only that notation is rewritten as the plain-language equivalent it already means, f = s - g. Nothing is dropped and it is 149 tokens versus 152.

Fresh rollouts under the incumbent scored 2/8 and four of the six failures died at the completion cap the same way: the student abandoned the literal row of labels for an index-to-index map, could not decide whether a slot sends or receives, derived a cycle structure that then contradicted its own written row, and spent thousands of tokens relitigating that contradiction instead of counting. The incumbent's 'if two of your own passes disagree, settle the convention once and move on' is the inert clause: every rollout detects the disagreement and none settles it. I replace it with the concrete first move that prevents the ambiguity from arising at all, keep the count-until-return loop and the composite clause that successes rely on, and hold length at the incumbent's 106 tokens.
